I bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80 (filled at $222.80, ~$9,803 total), which sits within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps and leaves the $50,000 cash balance otherwise untouched — no funds were moved out of the account.

**Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results, confirming via Apple's newsroom and SEC EDGAR's Form 10-K for fiscal 2024 (ended September 28, 2024) that total net sales were $391.0B, net income $93.7B, diluted EPS $6.08, and operating income $123.2B, with Q4 revenue of $94.9B up 6% year over year (the year included a one-time $10.2B tax charge). I discarded a third-party "10-K mirror" site that reported materially wrong figures ($361.2B revenue, $79.4B net income, $5.12 EPS) — a good reminder to verify against primary filings. Recent news was neutral-to-slightly-positive, with shares around $222.70 as analysts weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout. Given solid revenue growth, strong profitability, and a price near the current market, I placed a single buy limit order at $222.80 (just above the $222.72 ask) for 44 shares, roughly $9,803 — comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order limit and well under the $20,000 daily cap, with the remaining cash left in the account.
